lead.t: It details various vascular ectasias, distinguishes between benign and malignant vascular tumours, and explores intermediate forms like Kaposi Sarcoma and Bacillary Angiomatosis.
lead.s: VASCULAR PATHOLOGY — Must-Know Comprehensive Notes — Notes

b: Bartonella henselae — transmitted by cat scratch or bite → cat-scratch disease in immunocompetent hosts (necrotising granulomatous lymphadenopathy)
Bartonella quintana — transmitted by body louse → trench fever in WWI; causes bacillary angiomatosis in AIDS patients
Bacillary angiomatosis: exclusively in immunocompromised hosts (AIDS, transplant recipients)
Bartonella infects endothelial cells → triggers HIF-1α → VEGF upregulation → vascular proliferation
HIF-1α activation is the key molecular mechanism explaining the vascular proliferative response.

b: Vascular proliferation in immunocompromised hosts (especially AIDS patients )
Caused by opportunistic bacilli of the Bartonella family
Bartonella henselae — reservoir = domestic cat; causes cat-scratch disease (necrotising granulomatous lymphadenopathy) in immunocompetent hosts
Bartonella quintana — transmitted by human body lice; caused trench fever in World War I
Lesions involve skin, bone, brain, and other organs

qs.q: In bacillary angiomatosis, which Bartonella species is associated with cat-scratch disease in immunocompetent hosts and has the domestic cat as its reservoir?
qs.e: Bartonella henselae is transmitted by cats and causes cat-scratch disease. Bartonella quintana is transmitted by body lice and caused trench fever.

qs.q: What is the primary mechanism by which Bartonella bacteria induce vascular proliferation in bacillary angiomatosis?
o: Stimulation of T-cell mediated immune response causing granuloma formation
Secretion of viral cyclin D homologues that inhibit p53
Induction of host tissue production of HIF-1α, which drives VEGF production
Direct destruction of endothelial cells leading to compensatory hyperplasia
qs.e: Bartonella induces HIF-1α production in host tissues, which drives VEGF production and subsequent vascular proliferation. Viral cyclin D is associated with HHV8/KS.
